findings.evidence: This is a **process** skill: a fixed sequence — read, checklist, edit-or-escalate per finding, summarize — not a body of standing knowledge to browse.
findings.fix: The self-classification serves a rubric reader more than the executing agent; keep only the operative reading order or drop the sentence and record the removal.

findings.evidence: The strategy-judgment test is stated twice: 'Does resolving this require a strategy or design judgment...' (line 27) and again as Escalation condition 1 (line 57), so the agent processes the same criterion at two checkpoints.
findings.fix: Keep the full trigger list only under '## Escalation conditions' and have the ask-yourself question point to that list instead of restating the criterion.

findings.evidence: The description gives WHAT and WHEN but no negative boundary against the near-miss neighbour that produces the reports, so 'review my design doc' style prompts may false-trigger it.
findings.fix: Append to the description: 'Not for producing review reports or running the review itself — only for applying an existing report's findings to the flagged documents.'

findings.evidence: Queries vary phrasing and include strong near-misses, but none carry the realism cues the trigger-eval guide recommends: file paths, personal context or backstory.
findings.fix: Rewrite 3-4 queries per side with realistic paths and context, e.g. 'The reviewer flagged my plan at ~/git/kit/.planning/plan-32.md — apply the findings and give me the Fix Summary.'

findings.evidence: 'If any input is missing, stop and ask. Do not guess paths.' has no Status spelling, while the Failure status is defined only for a document not on disk (line 20, 92) — a review report that is missing leaves the dispatched, non-interactive subagent without a parseable outcome.
findings.fix: Map a missing report path to `### Status: Failure — <reason>` (or an explicit Findings escalated line naming the missing input) so the orchestrator gets a contract-shaped outcome for every failed start.
